Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

import os,re,json
d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
    k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
    rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
    if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
        G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
# print demo 3 with colors, find the "special color" per grid (color other than bg that's not the line color)
def analyze(p):
    I=G[f'Demo pair {p} input']
    from collections import Counter
    cnt=Counter(x for r in I for x in r)
    print('pair',p,'counts',cnt.most_common())
    nonbg=[(i,j,I[i][j]) for i in range(len(I)) for j in range(len(I[0])) if I[i][j]!=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]]
    return set(x for _,_,x in nonbg)
print(analyze(1)); print(analyze(2)); print(analyze(3))

import os,re,json
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load(); print(sorted(G))

for p in [8]:

    H,W=len(I),len(I[0])
    cnt=Counter(x for r in I for x in r); bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    cc=components(I)
    singles={comp[0] for comp in cc if len(comp)==1}
    wallcells = {(r,c) for c in cc if len(c)>1 for r in c} - set(singles)
    # also non-bg non-wall non-single cells
    other = {(r,c) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if I[r][c]!=bg and (r,c) not in singles and (r,c) not in wallcells}
    print('=== pair',p,'bg',bg)
    print(' strays:',sorted(singles))
    print(' walls:',sorted(wallcells))
    print(' others:',sorted(other))
    for r in range(H):
        line=''.join('S' if (r,c) in singles else ('W' if (r,c) in wallcells else ('O' if (r,c) in other else '.')) for c in range(W))
        line2=''.join('C' if O[r][c]!=I[r][c] else '.' for c in range(W))
        print(line+' '+' '+line2)

def analyze(p):
    I=G[f'Demo pair {p} input']; O=G[f'Demo pair {p} output']
    H,W=len(I),len(I[0])
    cnt=Counter(x for r in I for x in r); bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    singles=[c for c in components(I) if len(c)==1]
    walls=[c for c in components(I) if len(c)>1]
    ch=[]
    for i in range(H):
        for j in range(W):
            if I[i][j]!=O[i][j]:
                ch.append((i,j,I[i][j],O[i][j]))
    print('=== pair',p,'bg',bg)
    print(' markers:',[(str(I[s[0][0]][s[0][1]]),list(s)) for s in singles])
    for (i,j,a,b) in ch:
        ds=[abs(s[0][0]-i)+abs(s[0][1]-j) for s in singles]
        md=min(ds)
        cands=[s for s,d in zip(singles,ds) if d==md]
        # key: positions of candidate markers (as tuple of coords)
        pos=tuple(sorted([list(s)[0] for s in cands]))
        print(f'  ({i},{j}) {a}->{b} : nearest markers {pos}')

def label(p):
